issues.detail: The Hebrew phrase 'בַּחֲרֹשֶׁת הַגּוֹיִם' (in Harosheth-ha-goiim) is a proper place name, 'Harosheth of the nations/Gentiles', not '各民族' (all nations/peoples) as a generic description. The Chinese rendering '各民族的雕刻之地' (the carved place of all nations) misinterprets the proper noun 'חֲרֹשֶׁת' (Harosheth) as '雕刻' (carving/engraving) and 'הַגּוֹיִם' (the nations) as a generic '各民族', losing the place-name identity and adding a meaning not in the Hebrew.
